notices.Description:
This Contract Details Notice relates to 'Lot 8 (Cleaning and Maintenance)' 
Please note that this opportunity was seeking to establish a series of open Framework Agreements. Each successive open framework will be for specific products and/or services that will be awarded to successful suppliers, pursuant to which the Participating Authorities listed in Annex 1 of the Procurement Specific Questionnaire may award a Call-Off Agreement. 
It is has been awarded to the top 3 successful suppliers at the time of publication of this notice 2 Supplies have completed their respective Framework Agreement with the other to be added.   Participating Authorities will be able to enter into a Call-Off Agreement under the Framework Agreement following the call-off procedure.  Access to the documentation can be found here https://ccaps.bluelightcommercial.police.uk/login/index.php
Asan open framework it is intended that it will have a maximum term of 8 years. It is anticipated that the successive frameworks will re-open as follows: in (i) July 2029 and (ii) between July 2032 and July 2033. These dates may be subject to change at the discretion of the Contracting Authority. Anyone wishing to take part should look for further notices to be published around these times.

notices.Title: Closed Tender - Concessionary Contract for Activation of tennis facilities within Oldham Parks
notices.Title Compact: Closed Tender - Concessionary Contract for Activation of tennis facilities within Oldham Parks
notices.Description:
The cost for this Service will be commissioned based, with 50% of the income being paid to the Operator. The Club spark booking system is currently in use within the Service and costs a fixed amount of £500 per annum. 
The management and launch of the Club Spark booking system. 
The  operator will be fully responsible for driving all on court activity maximising:  
•	Annual membership / season ticket uptakes  
•	Pay & Play courts and bookings  
•	Coaching programmes to engage a variety of our communities including those that face the most inequalities, encouraging more players on to court 
•	LTA recognised schemes that encourage participation (including Local tennis leagues, Free Tennis Offer, Cardio tennis etc)  
•	Establish a schools tennis programme in conjunction with key local education leads including the local School Games Organiser (SGO) 
•	Introduction of a disability programme (Walking tennis, Wheelchair tennis, etc)  
•	Building links with other community groups to advertise tennis opportunities and increase tennis take-up in harder to reach communities

notices.Title: Weighbridge upgrades for digital waste tracking at Warwickshire Household Waste Recycling Centres (HWRCs)
notices.Title Compact: Weighbridge upgrades for digital waste tracking at Warwickshire Household Waste Recycling Centres (HWRCs)
notices.Description:
Warwickshire County Council is a Waste Disposal Authority, responsible for arranging the disposal of municipal waste collected within the county and for providing Household Waste Recycling Centres (HWRCs). Four of the Council-operated HWRCs (Lower House Farm, Princes Drive, Hunters Lane, and Burton Farm) have weighbridges. The weighbridges play a critical role in ensuring the compliant management of municipal waste across Warwickshire. The weighbridges enable the accurate measurement of waste loads from a wide range of vehicles, waste types, and stakeholders. They also support the provision of waste transfer documentation, ensuring legal compliance.
The current weighbridge infrastructure supplied by Weightron has been in place since at least 2011 following the Council's takeover of HWRC operations and has been consistently supported by Weightron since that time.
The proposed works will be delivered through a single supplier arrangement with Weightron, as the current provider of the Council's weighbridge infrastructure and software. The works relate to the Council's statutory responsibilities as a Waste Disposal Authority, including the operation of HWRCs and the compliant management of municipal waste.
The weighbridge service is currently operating effectively, however there is a new requirement to implement Digital Waste Tracking as mandated by DEFRA. The Government's intention is for this system to replace paper-based waste transfer documentation with a single, centralised digital platform for recording all waste movements helping to improve traceability and reduce waste crime.
From October 2026 it becomes mandatory for all permitted waste receiving sites to submit information about the commercial waste they receive onto DEFRA's new digital waste tracking system. This includes the HWRCs operated by the Council. There will be a second phase to DEFRA's digital waste tracking project from October 2027. This contract covers implementation (including setup/configuration), software development and annual subscriptions for the contract lifespan for both phases.
In order to comply with digital waste tracking requirements, Weightron must carry out works to ensure that all required waste receipt information is captured through the weighbridge system and automatically reported to the national digital waste tracking service.
There is a current contract in place for the weighbridges which includes servicing, maintaining, upgrading, and repairing the weighbridge equipment and hardware systems as well as providing software support. The total term of this contract is 10 years however, this is reviewed annually and 3 months' notice can be given to end the agreement. Weightron currently provides all of this service. The existing provision and the new digital waste tracking requirements must be delivered by the same supplier to ensure full integration with the existing weighbridge infrastructure and hardware.

notices.Title: Kent Grazing Project – Infrastructure Works
notices.Title Compact: Kent Grazing Project – Infrastructure Works
notices.Description:
North Kent Grazing Project – Infrastructure Works (Contract Ref: CN260754) 
Kent County Council (KCC) is seeking to appoint a suitably experienced contractor to deliver infrastructure works for the North Kent Grazing Project, a landscape-scale nature recovery initiative supporting the restoration and long-term management of chalk grassland and associated habitats across sites within and surrounding the Kent Woods and Downs National Nature Reserve (NNR).  
The project forms part of the delivery of the Kent and Medway Local Nature Recovery Strategy (LNRS) and aims to reintroduce and support conservation grazing across multiple sites to improve the condition of chalk grassland, woodland edge and scrub mosaic habitats, enhance habitat connectivity, reduce scrub encroachment and support long-term sustainable land management.  
KCC requires a contractor capable of delivering a coordinated package of conservation-sensitive infrastructure works across several sites in North Kent between Autumn 2026 and Autumn 2027.  
The scope of works includes: 
Stock-proof fencing installation, with some sites requiring removal of dilapidated fencing 
Supply and installation of field gates, deer gates and accessibility gates, as specified in the brief. 
Scrub clearance and green waste management, including mulching. 
Water infrastructure installation, including pipework, troughs and connections to existing water supplies. 
Construction of access tracks where required.  
The works will be undertaken across multiple locations including Birling Estate, Ranscombe Farm Reserve, Trosley Country Park, Shorne Woods Country Park and Ladds Farm, many of which are designated Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs) and all of which lie within the Kent Downs National Landscape and the North Kent Woods and Downs National Nature Reserve.  
The supplier must be able to demonstrate: 
Experience delivering fencing and land-based infrastructure works in environmentally sensitive locations. 
Ability to work safely and effectively within protected landscapes and designated sites, meeting the necessary conservation criteria required for protected sites. 
Appropriate machinery and equipment for challenging terrain and ecological constraints. 
Capacity to deliver works across multiple sites within the programme timeframe. 
Compliance with all relevant legislation, British Standards and health and safety requirements. 
Relevant accreditations and competent, suitably qualified operatives.  
Due to the variation in terrain, access requirements and site conditions, site visits are mandatory and will be coordinated upon expression of interest.  
This contract comprises a single lot and will be awarded on the basis of the lowest priced compliant tender, subject to meeting the quality requirements set out within the procurement documentation.  
The anticipated contract period is between Autumn/Winter 2026 and  Autumn 2027, with works funded through the Farming in Protected Landscapes (FiPL) Programme.  
The closing date for submission of quotations is 12:00 noon on 28th August 2026.
For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: 
https://www.kentbusinessportal.org.uk/tenders/UK-UK-Maidstone:-Environmental-improvement-works./5Y59TS653C
To respond to this opportunity, please click here: 
https://www.kentbusinessportal.org.uk/respond/5Y59TS653C

notices.Description:
The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) wish to give notice of planned procurement opportunity in relation to two linked but separate future procurements for DWP payment contingency services (together referred to in this notice as the “Payment Contingency Services (“PCS”)).   
The intention of the PCS is to ensure DWP has robust contingencies in place to make benefit and pension entitlement payments to its customers on the dates they are due. The PCS are invoked only in exceptional circumstances where there is a delay in DWP releasing Bacs payment file(s).   
The DWP intends for the relevant services to be provided under two separate, interdependent contracts (both of which are required to allow for invocation of PCS) as follows:  
Short Term Payment Contingency (“STPC”) - Lot 1: This service reformats Bacs payments files into Faster Payment files for onward submission into the Faster Payment infrastructure   
Sponsor Bank (“SB”) – Lot 2: This service is required for the settlement of funds with the Bank of England.   
Please note that as these are separate procurements, different procurement processes and/or commercial approach may apply to each procurement. In addition, each procurement may be awarded, delayed, or withdrawn independently of the other.   
This notice relates specifically to the SB procurement. A separate UK3 Planned Procurement Notice has been issued for the STPC procurement, which can be found on Find a Tender Service.   
Please note that:  
- Further information and relevant guidance will be provided in or with the UK4 Tender Notice, published on Find a Tender Service website. 
- UK 4 Notice and associated procurement documents provided with that notice will outline how and when to express your interest to participate in the procurement process. 
- All procurement activities will be managed via DWP online portal (Atamis).  
- Procurement related documentation will be issued via Atamis. Full guidance on registration and system navigation will be provided in or with the UK4 Notice. 
- It is mandatory for any interested suppliers to register on the new Central Digital Platform (CDP) which is part of the enhanced Find a Tender Service in order to participate in any future procurements. Details of how to register will be included in or with the UK4 Notice. 
- The DWP will not be liable for any expenditure, work, or effort incurred by a provider in acting based on this notice.  
- The information provided in this notice is for indicative purposes only. The DWP reserves its rights to amend any of the information included in the notice. 
- DWP reserves the right to add or remove stages throughout the procurement process or to reduce the tendering period in future (in accordance with the PA 23). The DWP also reserves the right to decide not to proceed with this procurement.  
- Please note, that involvement in Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) which was taking place 12/05/2026 or the One-to-One supplier events taking place between 01/06/2026 and 05/06/2026 are not a pre-requisite for participating in the procurement process. Please see the following link to the UK2 PME Notices for both STPC and SB - Short Term Payment Contingency Service - Find a Tender  and Sponsor Bank Service - Find a Tender . 
- This procurement will be conducted using the new procurement regime – Procurement Act 2023​. 
- It is currently anticipated that this procurement will follow a one stage Competitive Flexible Procedure.

notices.Title: Rainwater Management
notices.Title Compact: Rainwater Management
notices.Description: United Utilities (UU) wishes to engage the market to support the delivery of Rainwater Management schemes across the North West of England. The Environment Act and subsequent Storm Overflow Discharge Reduction Plan (SODRP) have introduced a statutory requirement to significantly reduce the operation of storm overflows, with all storm overflows expected to spill no more than ten times per year by 2050. Approximately 54% of United Utilities' wastewater network is a combined sewer system, conveying both surface water and wastewater to Wastewater Treatment Works (WwTWs) or Combined Sewer Overflows (CSOs) prior to discharge to the environment. This framework will enable United Utilities to appoint Contractors to deliver Rainwater Management solutions that reduce the volume of surface water entering the combined sewer network. Through the implementation of nature-based and sustainable drainage interventions, the framework aims to mitigate the impacts of storm overflows, improve network resilience, and contribute to the achievement of regulatory and environmental objectives. United Utilities’ (UU) Rainwater Management strategy is founded on Sustainable Drainage principles, which prioritise the capture, reuse and management of rainwater as close as possible to where it falls. The strategy promotes the use of surface conveyance, infiltration, disconnection and attenuation to slow the movement of water through the catchment and reduce pressure on the wastewater network. This approach, combined with measures to improve water efficiency, creates additional capacity within wastewater catchments, reduces demand for potable water, and maximises value by delivering wider environmental, social and economic benefits through the creation of blue-green infrastructure. By increasing the use of Rainwater Management interventions, UU can reduce its reliance on traditional, carbon-intensive engineering solutions, such as underground storage tanks, while delivering best value outcomes for customers and the environment. Whilst many of the individual interventions are well-established and proven, the scale and pace of delivery proposed by UU is unprecedented within the sector. The opportunity lies in developing and deploying these solutions at scale, working collaboratively with customers, businesses, Local Authorities, and other key stakeholders to drive widescale delivery and maximise catchment-wide benefits. The current Rainwater Management Programme identifies approximately 6,500 interventions across the United Utilities network area. However, Bidders should note that the programme remains subject to ongoing development and refinement may include up to 10,000 interventions over the framework term. Interventions will be delivered across the five county areas served by United Utilities: Cumbria, Lancashire, Cheshire, Greater Manchester and Merseyside. Particular focus is anticipated within Greater Manchester and Merseyside over AMP8, reflecting the strategic importance of these areas, the presence of Combined Authorities, and the objectives set out within their respective Integrated Water Management Plans (IWMPs). Rainwater Management Intervention Types Attenuation Pond: holding water body, suitable in large natural spaces only Bio-retention: pollution control incorporated into intervention design Blue Roof: smart water storage to catch rainwater and slow the return period Disconnection: surface water systems or extraneous rainwater from the combined network to a more suitable receiver e.g. water course. Downpipe Disconnection: from residential and business buildings, e.g. butt rainwater planter. Filter Drain: trench filled with gravel, water infiltrates to ground Green roofs: water retaining layer beneath a growing medium and planting for additional benefits e.g. air quality, biodiversity. Natural Flood Management (NFM): landscape solutions to manage uplands to retain rainwater where it falls e.g. leaky dams, catchment planting Permeable Paving: water infiltrates to ground or stored/ attenuated underground Rain Garden: surface planting, water infiltrates to ground or stored/ attenuated underground Soakaway: excavation filled with gravel and landscaped. Water infiltrates to ground Swale: shallow wide channel to catch, slow the flow or infiltrate water to ground. Can be wet and/ or dry Tree Pit: underground system combining urban tree planting with drainage that captures stormwater Landscape Maintenance & Management: services to undertake appropriate landscape maintenance such as mowing, watering, visual inspections, re-planting, silt removal. Disconnections Contractors will be responsible for the Design and Build of low complexity surface water disconnection works, where existing surface water pipes connected to the combined sewer network will be diverted to a more suitable receiving system. This may include connection to existing surface water sewers, or discharge via Rainwater Interventions such as rain gardens, attenuation ponds etc. Minor Works Streets Contractors will be responsible for the Design and Build of Rainwater Management interventions located within highways. These will comprise of non-complex standardised design solutions; however, Contractors will be expected to apply appropriate design judgement, innovation and technical capability to adapt solutions to site-specific constraints, stakeholder requirements and opportunities for wider environmental or placemaking benefits. The Contractor will be responsible for managing Traffic Management and gaining the necessary consents/ permits/ license, therefore holding the necessary Street Works Qualifications. In addition, demonstrate the appropriate balance of technical capability and relevant experience to successfully deliver nature-based solutions, encompassing both civil engineering and green infrastructure/landscape expertise. Minor Works – Five S’s Contractors will be responsible for the design and build of Rainwater Management interventions on private sites with a specific focus on schools, supermarkets, stations, state buildings (e.g. hospitals), and social housing sites. Solutions are expected to be low complexity to support delivery at pace and may range from product-based interventions through to bespoke site-specific designs. Contractors will need to consider practical delivery constraints within live environments, such as school playgrounds, supermarket car parks, hospital estates and residential settings. In addition to improving rainwater management, successful solutions should seek to deliver wider social, environmental and community benefits by creating attractive, functional and usable spaces for the people who use them. Examples may include: Interactive and educational outdoor environments for schools Calming and attractive spaces that support wellbeing within healthcare settings Planted areas that improve local amenity and help promote a sense of community within social housing sites Major Works Contractors will be responsible soley for the delivery of the Works (construction) on complex packages comprising of multiple Rainwater Management Interventions across a range of typologies within a single scheme. Interventions may include, but are not limited to, permeable paving, rain gardens, swales, and detention basins. And could be located within highways, public open space, catchment land, public realm. Design services will be provided by others, either by United Utilities' in-house team or by Design Partners appointed through a separate United Utilities framework. The Contractor shall provide suitably qualified and experienced resources with the appropriate balance of civil engineering, green infrastructure, and landscape expertise also managing construction, to support the successful delivery of nature-based solutions in both rural and urban locations. Natural Flood Management (NFM) NFM requires specialist environmental contractors to design and build nature based solutions such as leaky dams, wetlands, earth bunds and catchment planting such as woodland buffer strips or sphagnum moss. Habitat restoration, hydraulic assessment and traditional land management construction capabilities are essential for success. Along with working within designated and highly protected landscapes and with sensitive land owners. Products & Manufacturing Suppliers will be required to manufacture, store, supply, deliver and, where required, install Rainwater Management products suitable for deployment across household and non-household settings. This may include products designed or specified by United Utilities, including those where United Utilities owns or controls the intellectual property, alongside supplier-proposed products or product developments. Products may include, but are not limited to, water butts, rainwater planters, SuDS planters, modular attenuation or storage products, and associated components. Suppliers shall demonstrate the ability of repeatability and delivery at scale in terms of manufacturing, storage, distribution arrangement and installation capability. Also, the ability to deliver in the UU technical, operational and customer environment. Surveys & Investigations Contractor will provide Survey Works to support the delivery of the Rainwater Management Programme. This will include, Topographical, Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) Drainage (Connectivity, CCTV, MH cards), Impermeable Area Survey (IAS), Contaminated Surface Water (CSW) for cross connections and infiltration tests (BRE 365)

notices.Title: 291 Harrow Road Housebuilder warranty
notices.Title Compact: 291 Harrow Road Housebuilder warranty
notices.Description:
Suppliers are encouraged to review the Preliminary market engagement document on the Jaggaer Portal. Further detail is below.
The requirement:
The Council requires a housebuilder warranty and insurance policy for the 291 Harrow Road development. The Council, acting as the developer, has appointed a main contractor to undertake pre-construction services and ultimately to construct three towers at the 291 Harrow Road site. In total the three towers will deliver 144 new homes. Construction is due to commence in late 2027.
Council requires a suitable warranty and insurance provider for the new build including cover for the works and structural warranty post-completion.
The requirement is for a 12-year policy, including the two-year defect liability period after the practical completion. It must cover both the private sale and social rent units.
The policy must protect purchaser deposits if the contractor becomes insolvent before completion, a warranty for the private sale building block (which is attached to an existing already insured Private Accommodation Building), and appropriate for both UK and overseas purchasers. 
Further detail on the opportunity and requirement are in a draft scope of services available to the market on the Council's Jaggaer eProcurement Portal (link below).
Preliminary market engagement:
The Council is commencing preliminary market engagement as of 10 August 2026. A preliminary market engagement document and questionnaire have been developed and are available for prospective tenderers, alongside a draft of the scope of services. 
The preliminary market engagement aims to gather information from the market to help inform the procurement process, and inform the Council's officers of potential suppliers in the market. The questionnaire consists of 12 questions for completion.
Jaggaer eProurement Portal:
The documents are available on the Council's Jaggaer eProcurement Portal via the following link (or using reference SQ_30217):
- https://wcc.ukp.app.jaggaer.com/go/00056550019FC8372C13
Suppliers can register to the Portal here:

Deadline for preliminary market engagement:
The submission deadline for the preliminary market engagement is 26 August 2026. 
Procurement process to follow:
A summary of the procurement process for this opportunity is below (and is subject to change):
1. Preliminary market engagement stage to gauge interest from suppliers and gather information to help formulate the procurement process.
2. Initial tender stage to request formal responses from suppliers 
3. Initial evaluation stage to assess initial responses and determine acceptability of terms and conditions
4. Response stage to allow the Council to submit relevant information to suppliers for a quote
5. Quote stage where suppliers submit a quote to the Council

Further detail on the process can be found in the PME document.

notices.Title: NW3213 - RFID scanning for Scientific Services
notices.Title Compact: NW3213 - RFID scanning for Scientific Services
notices.Description:
Northumbrian Water Limited (NWL) is seeking market engagement with suppliers capable of delivering an RFID-based sample tracking solution for use within its laboratory operations.
The initial requirement is for a Proof of Concept (PoC) at one NWL laboratory site to assess the feasibility of replacing elements of the current barcode-based sample tracking process with RFID technology. The PoC will evaluate operational benefits, integration requirements and overall suitability before any decision is made regarding wider deployment across NWL's laboratory network.
The anticipated scope includes:
•	Assessment of infrastructure and technology requirements to support RFID-based sample tracking.
•	Provision of RFID tags, RFID-enabled printing capability, fixed and handheld scanning devices, and supporting software.
•	Installation and configuration of PoC equipment at one  laboratory.
•	Definition of integration requirements with NWL's Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS), Thermo SampleManager.
•	Support for test scenarios covering sample receipt, transfer, tracking and traceability processes.
•	Production of recommendations for future implementation should the PoC demonstrate a viable business case.
NWL currently envisages a future solution being capable of:
•	Printing RFID labels across multiple operational sites.
•	Integrating with Thermo SampleManager to maintain sample information and status updates.
•	Simultaneously scanning large volumes of sample bottles (target capability of at least 500 bottles at fixed scanning points).
•	Supporting handheld scanning throughout laboratory facilities and sampling operations.
•	Providing robust operation within laboratory environments, including cold storage areas and conditions involving moisture and chemical exposure.
•	Supporting future expansion opportunities, including chain-of-custody tracking, storage monitoring, inventory management and asset tracking.
The PoC will be assessed against a range of success criteria, including:
•	Improved sample traceability and reduced risk of lost or misplaced samples.
•	Reduction in unreadable labels and manual data entry.
•	Improved efficiency of sample receipt and processing activities.
•	Reliable integration with existing systems.
•	High levels of data security, availability and performance.
•	Scalability to support future deployment across multiple laboratory sites.
Suppliers with relevant experience and capability are invited to submit expressions of interest together with product literature, service overviews, case studies, technical specifications and any other supporting collateral that may assist NWL in understanding available market solutions.
Submissions and clarification questions should be sent to danielle.ruddick@nwl.co.uk. NWL may contact suppliers to request further information, clarification or follow-up discussions where appropriate. Following completion of this preliminary market engagement exercise, NWL intends to undertake a competitive procurement process informed by the findings of the engagement and associated PoC activities.
